rows.card: Stellar parallax measures distance from a star’s apparent shift as Earth changes position in its orbit. Nearby stars shift more than distant ones against the background. Knowing the observing baseline turns this tiny angular change into a geometric measurement rather than an estimate based on stellar brightness.

records.description: apparent shift of position of a nearby star against the background of distant objects during Earth's orbital period

rows.label: Stern–Gerlach experiment
rows.learning_takeaway: A nonuniform magnetic field splits a silver-atom beam into two bands rather than a classical continuum.
rows.card: The Stern–Gerlach experiment sent ground-state silver atoms through a nonuniform magnetic field and produced two separated bands. A classical picture allowing every magnetic orientation would predict a continuous spread. The result reveals quantized angular-momentum projections associated with the atoms’ unpaired electron spin.

records.description: physical experiment that demonstrated the quantization of angular momentum

rows.label: Thermocline
rows.learning_takeaway: Recognize a depth interval where temperature drops rapidly below a warm mixed surface layer.
rows.card: A thermocline is a layer where water temperature changes rapidly with depth, separating warmer surface water from colder water below. Its depth and strength vary with place and season. Recognizing the layer helps describe an ocean’s vertical structure instead of assuming its temperature is uniform.

records.description: distinct layer in a large body of fluid in which temperature changes more rapidly with depth than it does in the layers above or below

rows.label: Tidal force
rows.learning_takeaway: Differences in gravitational pull across an extended object create stretching and tidal effects.
rows.card: Tidal forces arise because gravity differs across an extended object. The side nearer an attracting body is pulled more strongly than the far side. Comparing each part’s acceleration with the object’s center explains stretching, ocean-tide patterns, and potentially the disruption of stars passing too close.

rows.label: Triple point
rows.learning_takeaway: Three phases coexist at one pressure-temperature combination on a pure-substance phase diagram.
rows.card: A pure substance’s triple point is the pressure and temperature where three phases coexist in equilibrium. On water’s phase diagram, it is where the solid–liquid, liquid–vapor, and solid–vapor boundaries meet. Below that pressure, liquid water is not an equilibrium phase.

records.description: thermodynamic point where three matter phases exist

rows.label: Warranties as quality assurance
rows.learning_takeaway: Shift specified repair or replacement obligations to a seller so buyers need not verify every quality claim beforehand.
rows.card: A warranty promises specified repair or replacement if a product fails within agreed conditions. It reduces the need for buyers to verify every aspect of quality before purchase by assigning some consequences to the seller. Its protection depends on the actual terms, rather than the label alone.

rows.label: Zheng He’s maritime expeditions
rows.learning_takeaway: Ming fleets projected imperial prestige and carried envoys through Indian Ocean networks rather than simply opening an unknown sea route.
rows.card: Zheng He’s Ming fleets traveled through established Indian Ocean networks carrying envoys and projecting imperial prestige. Their journeys connected diplomacy, trade and demonstrations of power. Understanding those purposes shifts attention from a simple story of discovering unknown places to the political relationships the voyages sought to organize.
